title: What the Asian Elephant carries

is_this_you.pressure: When bad news lands, your voice drops. The ones who matter feel it through the ground before they hear a word.
is_this_you.love: You love by provisioning. The fridge is full and the tire is fixed before anyone thinks to ask.
is_this_you.cost: You keep the white elephant. It costs more than it feeds you, and putting it down still feels like betrayal.

opener.text: On a second-century relief from Gandhara, now in the Metropolitan Museum, Queen Maya sleeps and dreams [s5]. A six-tusked elephant comes down from heaven and enters her right side, and the Buddha is conceived [s5]. Later tellings make the elephant white [s6]. You were born a Cancer in the year of the Ox, and like that dream elephant, you arrived already carrying someone.

howto: Three parts. Take them at walking pace.

tabs.label: The herd
tabs.intro: Water that feels everything. Earth that keeps walking.

rows.text: Cancer is cardinal Water, ruled by the Moon, the sign that builds a home and guards it [s1] [s2]. The Ox is yin Earth, patient and dependable [s3] [s4]. Earth holds Water in the five phases, so the Ox gives your tides banks to run between. You feel the whole load and keep walking.

Payne, Langbauer and Thomas recorded captive Asian elephants calling mostly between 14 and 24 hertz, at the bottom edge of human hearing and below it [s14]. Your strongest signals travel that low. A family feels your mood shift before you speak.

tabs.label: What you carry home
tabs.intro: Long days, full arms, seeds dropped far away.

rows.text: A wild Asian elephant spends about three quarters of its day eating or walking to food and water, taking in up to 150 kilograms of plants [s12] [s11]. Your days run that long. The Ox in you skips meals to finish the work [s4].

In Thailand and Myanmar white elephants are sacred and are presented to the king [s6]. A lesser white one could be handed to a rival, because it could not be worked and its keep could ruin the owner [s6]. That is your shadow. A duty nobody lets you set down.

About half the seeds an Asian elephant swallows travel more than 1.2 kilometres before they drop [s17]. What you plant lands far from you too. Nursing, elder care, trust work and archives all pay for stamina and a memory for who belongs.

tabs.label: Who you let into the herd
tabs.intro: Three who walk at your pace. One whose feet point elsewhere.
tabs.love_lead: In love you open slowly, with the Moon's need for a home and the Ox's slow warmth [s1] [s4]. You want someone who notices the load without being told. Tradition offers three herd-mates.

easy.why: The Pangolin (Taurus, Snake year) shares your trine of Ox, Snake and Rooster, and Taurus Earth gives your Water a bank [s3] [s1].
The Coconut Crab (Cancer, Rat year) is your secret friend, since the Rat is the Ox's hidden ally, and it shares your Cancer sun [s3].
The Slow Loris (Scorpio, Snake year) is trine kin through the Snake, and Scorpio is Water like you [s3] [s1].

hard.why: The hard one is the Hercules Beetle (Capricorn, Goat year): the Goat clashes with the Ox, and Capricorn sits opposite Cancer [s3] [s1].

story.text: The Records of the Three Kingdoms, 三國志 (Sānguózhì), tells how Sun Quan sent Cao Cao an elephant nobody could weigh [s10]. The boy Cao Chong led it onto a boat, marked the waterline, then loaded the boat with goods to the same mark and weighed those [s10]. The tale is 曹沖稱象 (Cáo Chōng chēng xiàng). Water measured the elephant. Your Moon side shows what the Ox has carried.

closing: Walk on at your own pace. The herd has always kept time by your feet.
